title: Explicit last-generator exterior-power assembly is bijective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $r,n\in\mathbb N$. Put $E=R^{(\operatorname{Fin}r)}$ and $E^+=R^{(\operatorname{Fin}(r+1))}$. Let $j:E\to E^+$ send the standard generator $e_i$ to $e_{i.\mathrm{castSucc}}$, and let $\ell=e_{\operatorname{last}r}$. For the exterior powers of [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], the explicitly constructed linear map $S_n:\Lambda^{n+1}E\oplus\Lambda^n E\to\Lambda^{n+1}E^+$, $S_n(a,b)=\Lambda^{n+1}(j)(a)+\iota(\ell)\Lambda^n(j)(b)$, is bijective. No regularity or nonzero-ring assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0628 (Lemma 15.29.7), proof identifying the cone terms by placing the new generator first; Tag 0629 (Lemma 15.29.8), specialization to the final generator of a finite sequence. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0628 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0629.

proof.text: Construct j by Finsupp.lmapDomain Fin.castSucc, and left wedge with the last generator by multiplication followed by restriction to exterior degree n+1. Membership follows from multiplication of powers of the generator submodule. Form S_n as the coprod of these two explicit linear maps.

Let p be restriction to the prefix and let δ evaluate the last coordinate. Prove p(j(v))=v, p(ell)=0 and j(p(v))+δ(v)ell=v by evaluating finitely supported vectors. Contraction δ kills the prefix exterior algebra by left induction, using the contraction recursion. The inverse in degree n+1 is x ↦ (Λ^(n+1)(p)x, Λ^n(p)(koszulBoundary δ x)); the degree restriction of contraction is supplied by the existing Koszul complex definition. Applying this inverse to S_n(a,b) recovers a and b, using p(ell)=0, contraction δ on the prefix equal to zero, and δ(ell)=1.

Set T=Λ(j)∘Λ(p) and L=ι(ell). Left induction on the full exterior algebra proves T(x)+L*T(contractLeft δ x)=x. Scalars and sums are immediate. For ι(v)*x, write ι(v)=ι(j(p(v)))+δ(v)L. Apply the contraction recursion and the induction hypothesis. Anticommutation moves L past ι(j(p(v))); L²=0 removes the extra last-generator term. Restrict to degree n+1 to show S_n applied to its proposed inverse is the identity. The two identities prove bijectivity over every commutative ring, also in rank zero or above the rank.

proof_origin.place: Explicit projection-and-contraction inverse refining the degreewise identification in Stacks Tag 0628.
